tool.name: MLST typing
tool.description: sequence type from assemblies against PubMLST and EnteroBase schemes
tool.command: python '$__tool_directory__/mlst_typing.py' --db '$__tool_directory__/database' --fofn '$fofn' --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} #if $scheme_mode.mode == 'force' --scheme '$scheme_mode.scheme' $scheme_mode.legacy #else --minscore $scheme_mode.minscore #if str($scheme_mode.exclude).strip() --exclude '$scheme_mode.exclude' #end if #end if $full #if str($full) and str($allele_layout) == 'combined' --combine-alleles #end if --minid $adv.minid --mincov $adv.mincov #if $adv.want_json --json '$json_out' #end if #if $adv.want_novel --novel '$novel_out' #end if --outfile '$report' --outfile-pubmlst '$report_pubmlst' --outfile-enterobase '$report_enterobase'

param.name: input
param.label: Assemblies
param.help: One or more assemblies (FASTA, GenBank or EMBL), or a collection. Sample names come from the dataset/element names.

param.name: minscore
param.label: Minimum score to report a scheme

param.name: scheme
param.label: Scheme name
param.help: For example saureus, spyogenes, neisseria, salmonella, ecoli_achtman_4.

param.name: legacy
param.label: Legacy layout (one column per locus with a header row)

param.name: full
param.label: Detailed output (header row, STATUS and SCORE)

param.name: allele_layout
param.label: Allele layout
param.help: Used by the detailed output. Schemes have 3 to 10 loci; with one column per allele, columns a scheme does not use stay empty.
param.option: One column per allele (ALLELE1 to ALLELE10)

param.name: minid
param.label: Minimum % identity of a full-length allele for a '~' call

param.name: mincov
param.label: Minimum % coverage for a partial '?' call

tool.help:
**What it does**
Finds the PubMLST and EnteroBase schemes that fit each assembly best and reports the **sequence type (ST)** and per-locus alleles. It checks every scheme in the bundled database at once, so you do not need to know the species.
Each assembly is typed against **PubMLST** (the main source) and, separately, against the **EnteroBase** 7-gene schemes (*Escherichia*, *Salmonella*, *Yersinia*, *Moraxella*), which hold newer STs. The report shows the PubMLST result; when PubMLST has no ST and EnteroBase has one, the EnteroBase result is shown and WARNINGS says so.
mlst-typing is a Python redesign of Torsten Seemann's *mlst*: same method, same allele notation and output, rebuilt in Python with a database updater that follows current PubMLST schemes.
**Allele calls**
========= =========================================================== ``N`` exact match to allele N ``~N`` full length, not exact; closest is N (possible novel allele) ``N?`` partial match to allele N (coverage ≥ mincov) ``-`` allele missing ``N,N`` several copies of the same exact allele (multi-copy locus) ``N,M`` different exact alleles (possible contamination) ========= ===========================================================
**Detailed output columns**
FILE, SCHEME, ST, ALLELE1 to ALLELE10, STATUS, SCORE (out of 100), WARNINGS.
Each ALLELE column holds one locus and its call, for example ``gki(4)``. Schemes have 3 to 10 loci; a scheme with 7 loci fills ALLELE1 to ALLELE7 and leaves ALLELE8 to ALLELE10 empty, so STATUS, SCORE and WARNINGS are always in the same columns. With **Allele layout** set to "Combined in one column" the alleles are in a single ALLELES column instead, joined with ``;`` (``gki(4);gtr(3);...``), as in versions before 0.3.0.
STATUS: PERFECT (full ST), PARTIAL (all loci found, some not exact, no ST), NOVEL (all alleles exact but a new combination), MULTICOPY (a locus in several copies of the same allele; the ST is still reported), MIXED (different exact alleles at one locus, no ST), MISSING (at least one allele missing, ``-``), BAD (score under 70), NONE (no scheme). The original mlst calls PARTIAL "OK" and reports MULTICOPY as MIXED without an ST.
**Outputs**
- **Report**: PubMLST and EnteroBase combined (use this one). - **PubMLST only** and **EnteroBase only**: what each source gives on its own, in the same layout. EnteroBase scheme names end in ``_enterobase``.
**How to read the report (WARNINGS column)**
SCHEME, ST, the alleles, STATUS and SCORE always come from the source shown in the row. "ST" below means a numbered ST (STATUS PERFECT, or MULTICOPY with an ST). "Same scheme" means the two schemes have the same loci.
.. csv-table:: :header: "#", "PubMLST", "EnteroBase", "Row shows", "WARNINGS" :widths: 3, 14, 20, 12, 51
1, "ST", "no scheme", "PubMLST", "(empty)" 2, "ST", "same scheme, same ST", "PubMLST", "(empty)" 3, "ST", "same scheme, different ST", "PubMLST", "``EnteroBase differs: <scheme> (ST<n>)``" 4, "ST", "same scheme, no ST", "PubMLST", "(empty)" 5, "ST", "different scheme", "PubMLST", "(empty); see the EnteroBase-only report" 6, "scheme, no ST", "ST", "EnteroBase", "``EnteroBase ST, no PubMLST (PubMLST: <scheme> <STATUS>)``" 7, "no scheme", "ST", "EnteroBase", "``EnteroBase ST, no PubMLST (PubMLST: NONE)``" 8, "scheme, no ST", "scheme, no ST", "PubMLST", "``No ST: PubMLST <STATUS>, EnteroBase <scheme> <STATUS>``" 9, "scheme, no ST", "no scheme", "PubMLST", "``No ST: PubMLST <STATUS>, EnteroBase NONE``" 10, "no scheme", "scheme, no ST", "PubMLST (``-``, NONE)", "``No ST: PubMLST NONE, EnteroBase <scheme> <STATUS>``" 11, "no scheme", "no scheme", "PubMLST (``-``, NONE)", "``No ST: PubMLST NONE, EnteroBase NONE``"
In case 6 the row is an EnteroBase scheme; check that the PubMLST scheme named in the warning is the same organism (EnteroBase's *E. coli* scheme also holds STs of other species).
WARNINGS can also hold ``TIE: scheme (STx), scheme (STy)`` when more than one scheme of the source shown gets the same top score. The first scheme by name is reported in SCHEME/ST (the original mlst picks one of them at random); check the tied schemes and use the one for your species. Several warnings are joined with ``;``. WARNINGS is also the last column of the default layout. With a forced scheme only that scheme is typed and the two sources are not compared.
**Database**
Allele and profile definitions from PubMLST (https://pubmlst.org) and BIGSdb-Pasteur: the standard, freely available data, submitted up to 31 December 2024. EnteroBase schemes (https://enterobase.warwick.ac.uk): current data from its public scheme downloads, for academic use; please cite EnteroBase when you report an EnteroBase ST.
